# Feature: Chain switch — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #28 (Chain switch) from Switches and Doors before it is used in real levels. Effect: switches must fire in order. Unique: the sequence matters, not just pressing them all. Useful: an order and memory puzzle across a room. Source status in the candidate file is 'trial'.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** switches must fire in order.

**So that** an order and memory puzzle across a room.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Chain switch for the first time in its teaching room (mech-28-chain-switch-room). Teaching moment: First room: three switches with clear order marks and an info tile beside the first. A player who presses the nearest switch first because it is nearest resets the chain and lights nothing, which teaches that the order, rather than the pressing, is the puzzle. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Switches carry order marks
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Pressing them in order lights each in turn and opens the linked door at the last one
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Pressing out of order resets all of them

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Chain switch's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-28-chain-switch-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/switches-and-doors.yml mechanic #28.
